question: You toss four fair coins. What is the probability that at least one head appears, given that not all coins show the same face?
explanation:
Let $E$: At least one head appears
Let $F$: Not all coins show the same face
Total outcomes: $2^4 = 16$
$P(F)$: All heads (1 way), all tails (1 way), so $n(F) = 16 - 2 = 14$

$E \cap F$: At least one head, but not all coins show same face (so, all tails case excluded)
Outcomes with at least one head: $16 - 1 = 15$ (exclude all tails)
But exclude the case with all heads, which is both all heads and at least one head (already excluded in $F$)
So, $E \cap F$ = $15 - 1 = 14$ (all but the case of all tails and all heads)

But with the definition, all cases except all tails (at least one head) and all heads (all H)
So, $E \cap F = n(F)$ = 14

So $P(E|F) = \frac{14}{14} = 1$

So, the answer is $\boxed{1}$.
